hints: Set up equilibrium equations: resolve horizontally $\sum F_x = 0$ to express $P\cos\theta$, and vertically $\sum F_y = 0$ to express $P\sin\theta$.
Divide the vertical equation by the horizontal equation to find $\tan\theta$, and use Pythagoras $P = \sqrt{(P\cos\theta)^2 + (P\sin\theta)^2}$ to find $P$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the exact trigonometric ratios for angle $\alpha$:
Given $\tan\alpha = \frac{7}{24}$, construct a right-angled triangle with opposite side 7, adjacent side 24, and hypotenuse $\sqrt{7^2 + 24^2} = \sqrt{49 + 576} = \sqrt{625} = 25$:
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{7}{25} = 0.28, \quad \cos\alpha = \frac{24}{25} = 0.96$$

Step 2: Resolve all forces horizontally for equilibrium (forces to the right balance forces to the left):
$$P\cos\theta + 14\sin\alpha = 48\cos\alpha$$
$$P\cos\theta = 48\cos\alpha - 14\sin\alpha$$
$$P\cos\theta = 48(0.96) - 14(0.28) = 46.08 - 3.92 = 42.16\text{ N}$$

Step 3: Resolve all forces vertically for equilibrium (upward forces balance downward forces):
$$P\sin\theta + 48\sin\alpha + 14\cos\alpha = 50$$
$$P\sin\theta = 50 - 48\sin\alpha - 14\cos\alpha$$
$$P\sin\theta = 50 - 48(0.28) - 14(0.96) = 50 - 13.44 - 13.44 = 50 - 26.88 = 23.12\text{ N}$$

Step 4: Determine the angle $\theta$ by dividing the vertical and horizontal components:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{P\sin\theta}{P\cos\theta} = \frac{23.12}{42.16} \approx 0.548387$$
$$\theta = \arctan(0.548387) \approx 28.74^\circ \approx 28.7^\circ$$

Step 5: Calculate the magnitude $P$ using the Pythagorean theorem on perpendicular components:
$$P = \sqrt{(P\cos\theta)^2 + (P\sin\theta)^2} = \sqrt{42.16^2 + 23.12^2}$$
$$P = \sqrt{1777.4656 + 534.5344} = \sqrt{2312.0} = 34\sqrt{2} \approx 48.083\text{ N} \approx 48.1\text{ N}$$
Thus, $P = 48.1\text{ N}$ and $\theta = 28.7^\circ$.
